source_cards.bounded_conclusion: Variable topology selection is promising under the published four-pseudo-stem protocol, but retrieval and mean similarity gains do not establish a universal rock-mixing rule.

knowledge_cards.claim: FX topology and ordering selection is distinct from parameter tuning inside a fixed chain.
Retrieval accuracy does not establish mix quality or preference.
Source-separated pseudo-stems inherit unmeasured separator artifacts.
Cross-song stem remixing reduces content shortcuts but breaks arrangement coherence.
Random effect chains do not encode genre- and role-dependent engineering practice.
Four broad stems are not equivalent to professional session-track granularity.
Balanced-window evaluation underrepresents sparse and role-changing sections.
Mean listener score without paired uncertainty or song dispersion is incomplete evidence.
Peak scaling before evaluation can hide gain and overload failures.
Finite-output wrapper tests do not establish effect semantics or production safety.
An empty processing chain must be verified as identity; clipping is a transformation.
